inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: §3.2 reports C_wide − C with its 20 dB interval, points to Table S9 for the other levels, and states the direction of the capacity control correctly (replacing B with B_wide adds to the advantage and removes none of it).

operationalization.fully_addressed: Read as the Journal-Fit seat (EIC); the check is D5 agreement between the §3.2 text and Table S9. Three elements in the §3.2 width-contrast paragraph (B0127 or its replacement), all required. (1) C_wide − C at 20 dB is reported with its interval, in the same statistic type the paragraph uses for D − B_wide (paired point estimate with its 95% interval; the reference values 38_ Residual Issue 3 gives are +0.034, CI −0.385 to +0.445, 28 of 58 seeds — the seed count is optional, the interval is not). (2) The paragraph says, with an explicit 'Table S9' pointer in the sentence that gives the 20 dB values or in the one next to it, that the per-level values of the width-only contrasts (B_wide − B and C_wide − C) at the other sweep levels where the advantage appears (35, 30 and 25 dB) are in Table S9. (3) The direction of the capacity control is stated correctly: the clause 'the capacity control removes 0.12 points of it at most', and any wording saying the widened control removes, reduces, absorbs or accounts for part of the advantage, is gone, and the replacement states that replacing B with B_wide adds to the advantage (by up to 0.12 points, B_wide − B being ≤ 0 at every level, −0.037 to −0.124 per Table S9) and removes none of it. Whether the paragraph also cites the regenerating script (tools/make_table_s9.py, mentioned in the suggested_action) is not part of the criterion and is noted, not scored.

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Both statements say fifty-four, matching the 54-entry list.

operationalization.fully_addressed: Read as the Journal-Fit seat (EIC). Two statements, both required: the §4.3 self-citation statement (B0060, formerly 'Three of the fifty-three references are to our own group') and the competing-interests statement (B0070, same count) each give the reference count as fifty-four (in words or as the numeral 54, in whatever form the sentence uses), neither still reads 'fifty-three' or '53', and the stated count equals the number of entries in the manuscript's own reference list, which 38_ records as 54 after Frerichs 2002 was added in round 3. If the two statements and the list agree on a count, the criterion is met; a statement that says fifty-four beside a list that no longer has 54 entries fails, because the criterion's test is 'matching the list', not the word itself. The numerator 'three' is not under test. The renderings in the submission file (36_ lines 164 and 300) are outside the manuscript and outside this criterion.

items.expected_change_surface: §4.3 B0060 and the competing-interests statement B0070; roadmap target_section '§4.3, Competing interests'. The reference-list length is the comparison surface.

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: The §1 sentence names the untested conditions or no longer claims that §4.4 names them.

operationalization.fully_addressed: Read as the Journal-Fit seat (EIC); the check is D5 cross-reference integrity. The §1 sentence (B0013 or its replacement) that reserves the companion conditions satisfies the criterion by either route. (a) It names the untested conditions in the sentence itself — the set the suggested_action lists is other reconstructors and noise models, the weighted loss, and measured data; naming the conditions §4.4 actually discusses as remaining suffices — with or without a pointer to §4.4. (b) It no longer claims that §4.4 names them ('The companion conditions are not tested here.' or equivalent), so that no cross-reference points at a list §4.4 does not contain. Under equivalence_policy the fix 38_ Residual Issue 8 offers at the other end also counts: if §4.4's closing sentence (B0062) now names the conditions so that the §1 pointer 'named in Section 4.4' resolves to an actual list, route (a) is met by position elsewhere. A §1 sentence that keeps 'named in Section 4.4' while §4.4 still ends 'The companion conditions remain to be tested' without naming them fails.

items.expected_change_surface: §1 B0013 one sentence; roadmap target_section '§1'. Alternative site under equivalence: §4.4 closing sentence B0062 (38_ Residual Issue 8).

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: No sentence in §4.1 or §4.2 apportions the benefit between the two readings or states that the mechanism's prediction fails in the matched condition; the matched condition is described as not tested.

operationalization.fully_addressed: Read as the methodology seat (R1). Three textual tests over every sentence of §4.1 and §4.2 as they stand, not only the two blocks the roadmap names; all three must pass. (a) Absence of apportionment: no sentence in §4.1 or §4.2 quantifies or ranks how much of the evaluation-only 20 dB benefit belongs to the training condition (mismatch tolerance) as against weak-component protection. In particular the §4.2 tail 'would have attributed to the branch what belongs mostly to the training condition' is gone, and no sentence in either section applies 'mostly', 'largely', 'mainly', 'predominantly', 'the larger part', 'the bulk' or 'most of' to the two readings. Wording that says the benefit did not survive training at the heavier level, or is attributable in whole or in part to shift tolerance, is not apportionment and passes. (b) Absence of a matched-condition refutation: no sentence in §4.1 or §4.2 says the mechanism's prediction fails, does not hold, is refuted, is contradicted or is falsified once training and evaluation are matched; the §4.1 clause 'this prediction does not hold once training and evaluation are matched' is replaced or removed. (c) Presence: §4.1 or §4.2 describes the matched condition as not tested (equivalents: 'not dissociated', 'receives no separate verdict', 'has no antecedent', 'was not tested because the component was no longer under threat'), with the reason the design supplies, namely that at matched training the control arm has recovered the component so it is no longer under threat by the paper's operational definition (control-arm loss). 'Refuted' and 'confirmed' both fail (c). The §3.5 measured-quantity sentence (B0123, 'Most of the gap ...') lies outside the sections the criterion names and is not scored under this item.

items.expected_change_surface: §4.2 sentence B0056 (apportioning tail) and §4.1 clause B0051; roadmap target_section '§4.1, §4.2'. Comparison surfaces, not expected change sites: §1 B0013 ('no separate verdict') and the §4.1 sentence 'the design cannot say which' (38_ Residual Issues 1–2).

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: §2.4 relates the 35 dB p to a Bonferroni threshold for seven levels; §2.6 lists D − B and the per-seed slope as unregistered; §3.1 marks D − B descriptive; §3.5 states that the shrinkage does not depend on the floor.

operationalization.fully_addressed: Read as the methodology seat (R1). Four statements, each in manuscript text or a table note (not the response letter), all required. (1) §2.4, beside the existing no-multiplicity-adjustment sentence: a clause that relates the sweep onset's 35 dB Wilcoxon p = 0.0011 to a Bonferroni threshold for the seven sweep levels (0.05/7 ≈ 0.0071) and says which side of it the p lies (below); saying only that the onset is read from seven correlated levels, without the threshold comparison, does not satisfy (1). (2) §2.6, in the list of analyses not pre-specified: the D − B contrast (the 40 dB paired difference carrying p = 0.041) and the per-seed slope (the 47-of-58 count) are both named as unregistered; naming them only in a table note or in §3.1 does not satisfy (2). (3) §3.1: wherever D − B is reported with its p-value (+0.191, p = 0.041), the same sentence or clause carries 'descriptive', 'unregistered', 'exploratory', 'not a registered test' or an equivalent label. (4) §3.5, beside the H5 verdict and the floor-SE statement: a clause stating that the 9.2-fold shrinkage of the 20 dB advantage (Δ_20|20 − Δ_20|40 = −1.868, CI −2.327 to −1.403, as 38_ Residual Issue 6 quotes it, or the same quantity in Dice points) does not depend on the floor, i.e. holds wherever the floor is set. The numbers quoted are the identification reference from 38_; values that recompute from the same per-seed files to the same rounding count as the same values.

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: §3.1 states that the contrast grows, not shrinks, when B_wide replaces B, with the correct values.

operationalization.fully_addressed: Read as the methodology seat (R1). The §3.1 sentence (B0037 or its replacement) that compares the 40|40 branch contrast against the two controls states that the contrast grows (increases, is larger) when the 38% larger B_wide replaces B; 'shrinks', 'falls', 'drops', 'narrows' and any synonym no longer describe that substitution. The values given agree with D − B = +0.191 and D − B_wide = +0.223 Dice points: either both differences, or the 0.03-point growth together with the +0.223 endpoint (e.g. 'grows by 0.03 points, to +0.223'), or wording equivalent in direction and magnitude. Direction and numbers must agree with each other and with the primary result reported elsewhere in §3.1 and Table 1 (D − B_wide +0.223). The 38% parameter figure may stay, since B_wide against B is 1.384; aligning its rounding with the Table S9 header's '+39% params' (38_ Residual Issue 5) is outside the inherited criterion and is noted, not scored.

items.expected_change_surface: §3.1 B0037 one clause; roadmap target_section '§3.1'. Table 1 and Table S9 (D − B +0.191, D − B_wide +0.223) are comparison surfaces, not expected change sites.
